Our ODE systems was as follows:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dx}{dt} &= rx\left(1-\frac{x}{K}\right) - axy - Hx \\
\frac{dy}{dt} &= bxy - my
\end{aligned}
$$
where x is prey population, y is predator population, r is prey growth rate, K is prey carrying
capacity, a is predation rate, b is predator growth efficiency, m is predator mortality rate,
and H is the human hunting quota.

```{r}
# Solves above deterministic ODE system until time T given initial conditions/parameters and plots
pred_prey_ode = function(D0, W0, r, K, a, H, b, m, T, step_size, title=''){
  
  f = function(t, s, params){
    x = s[1]
    y = s[2]
    return(list(c(r * x * (1 - x / K) - a * x * y - H * x, b * x * y - m * y)))
  }
  
  t = seq(0, T, step_size)
  out = ode(y=c(D0, W0), times=t, func=f, parms=NULL)

  
  plot(out[,1], out[,2], type='l', xlab='time (years)', ylab='prey', main=title)
  plot(out[,1], out[,3], type='l', xlab='time (years)', ylab='predator', main=title)
}

```

```{r}
# Simulates a run of the stochastic model until time T given parameters
pred_prey_mc = function(D0, W0, r, K, a, H, b, m, T){
  # event times
  S = c(0)
  # prey population
  D = c(D0)
  # predator population
  W = c(W0)
 
  d = D0
  w = W0
  v1 = r * d
  v2 = r * d^2 / K + a * w * d + H * d
  v3 = b * w * d
  v4 = m * w
  # used to simulate time until next birth/death event
  v = v1 + v2 + v3 + v4
  time = rexp(1, v)
  
  while (time <= T){
    S = c(S, time)
    # randomly determine which event type occurred e.g. prey birth
    u = runif(1, 0, 1)
    if (u <= v1 / v){
      d = d + 1
    } else if (u <= (v1 + v2) / v){
      d = d - 1
    } else if (u <= (v1 + v2 + v3) / v){
      w = w + 1
    } else {
      w = w - 1
    }
    
    D = c(D, d)
    W = c(W, w)
    # if both populations are extinct, then end simulation
    if (d == 0 && w == 0){
      break
    }
    
    # update expontential distribution constant
    v1 = r * d
    v2 = r * d^2 / K + a * w * d + H * d
    v3 = b * w * d
    v4 = m * w
    v = v1 + v2 + v3 + v4
    time = time + rexp(1, v)
  }

  return(list(S, D, W))
}

# Plots two runs of the stochastic model simulation
plot_mc = function(D0, W0, r, K, a, H, b, m, T, title=''){
  P1 = pred_prey_mc(D0, W0, r, K, a, H, b, m, T)
  P2 = pred_prey_mc(D0, W0, r, K, a, H, b, m, T)
  
  T1 = P1[[1]]
  T2 = P2[[1]]
  xmax = max(T1[length(T1)], T2[length(T2)])
  
  D1 = P1[[2]]
  D2 = P2[[2]]
  ymax = max(max(D1), max(D2))
  plot(T1, D1, type='l', col='red', xlim=c(0, xmax), 
       ylim=c(0, ymax), xlab='time (years)', ylab='prey', main=title)
  lines(T2, D2, col='blue')
  
  W1 = P1[[3]]
  W2 = P2[[3]]
  ymax = max(max(W1), max(W2))
  plot(T1, W1, type='l', col='red', xlim=c(0, xmax), 
       ylim=c(0, ymax), xlab='time (years)', ylab='predator', main=title)
  lines(T2, W2, col='blue')
}
```

```{r}
# find parameters for the model
moose = royal$moose
wolves = royal$wolves

# calculate differences to crudely estimate derivatives
delta_moose = rep(0, length(moose) - 1)
delta_wolves = rep(0, length(delta_moose))
for (i in 1:(length(moose) - 1)){
  delta_moose[i] = moose[i + 1] - moose[i]
  delta_wolves[i] = wolves[i + 1] - wolves[i]
}

moose = moose[1:length(delta_moose)]
wolves = wolves[1:length(delta_moose)]

# solve linear systems for parameter estimates
X = as.matrix(cbind(moose, moose^2, wolves * moose))
beta = solve(t(X) %*% X) %*% t(X) %*% delta_moose
r_hat = beta[1]
# prey carrying capacity, should be an integer
K_hat = round(-r_hat / beta[2], 0)
a_hat = -beta[3]

Y = as.matrix(cbind(wolves * moose, wolves))
beta = solve(t(Y) %*% Y) %*% t(Y) %*% delta_wolves
b_hat = beta[1]
m_hat = -beta[2]

r_hat
K_hat
a_hat
b_hat
m_hat
```

```{r}
# Monte Carlo simulates the stochastic model M times. Records how many times a population became extinct
# and calculates confidence intervals for probability of extinction.
prob_of_extinc = function(D0, W0, r, K, a, H, b, m, T, M){
  # prey survival
  X = rep(0, M)
  # predator survival
  Y = rep(0, M)
  
  for (i in 1:M){
    P = pred_prey_mc(D0, W0, r, K, a, H, b, m, T)
    D = unlist(P[2])
    W = unlist(P[3])
    n = length(D)
    # check if populations went extinct
    if (D[n] == 0){
      X[i] = 1
    }
    if (W[n] == 0){
      Y[i] = 1
    }
  }
  prey_p = mean(X)
  predator_p = mean(Y)

  prey_error = 1.96 * sd(X) / sqrt(M)
  prey_lower95 = max(0, prey_p - prey_error)
  prey_upper95 = min(1, prey_p + prey_error)
  
  predator_error = 1.96 * sd(Y) / sqrt(M)
  predator_lower95 = max(0, predator_p - predator_error)
  predator_upper95 = min(1, predator_p + predator_error)
  
  return(list(prey_p, prey_lower95, prey_upper95, predator_p, predator_lower95, predator_upper95))
}
```

```{r}
if(!require("foreach")) {install.packages("foreach")}
if(!require("doParallel")) {install.packages("doParallel")}

# determine number of cpu cores
n_cores <- detectCores()
# leave out one core
cluster = makeCluster(n_cores-1)
registerDoParallel(cluster)

# simulate stochastic model N times for multiple H values and record confidence intervals.
N = 50
hunting_values = seq(0.6, 0.75, by=0.025)
results = list()

results = foreach(i = 1:length(hunting_values)) %dopar% {
  prob_of_extinc(D0=moose[1], W0=wolves[1], r=r_hat, K=K_hat, a=a_hat, 
                 H=hunting_values[i], b=b_hat, m=m_hat, T=52, M=N)
}
stopCluster(cl = cluster)
```

```{r}
k = length(hunting_values)
prey_y = rep(0, k)
prey_lower = rep(0, k)
prey_upper = rep(0, k)

pred_y = rep(0, k)
pred_lower = rep(0, k)
pred_upper = rep(0, k)

for (i in 1:k){
  x = results[[i]]
  
  prey_y[i] = x[[1]]
  prey_lower[i] = x[[2]]
  prey_upper[i] = x[[3]]
  
  pred_y[i] = x[[4]]
  pred_lower[i] = x[[5]]
  pred_upper[i] = x[[6]]
}

plot(hunting_values, prey_y, xlim=c(hunting_values[1], hunting_values[k]), 
     ylim=c(0, 1), xlab='H', ylab='probability of prey extinction', cex=0.5)
arrows(hunting_values, prey_lower, hunting_values, prey_upper, length=0.05, angle=90, code=3)

plot(hunting_values, pred_y, xlim=c(hunting_values[1], hunting_values[k]), 
     ylim=c(0, 1), xlab='H', ylab='probability of predator extinction', cex=0.5)
arrows(hunting_values, pred_lower, hunting_values, pred_upper, length=0.05, angle=90, code=3)
```
